title: Patch fast-uri in the actual schema-validation consumer without changing application dependencies

source.ref: Current Dependabot alerts78-81 and upstream fast-uri advisories,2026-10-25

detail: Root lock resolved fast-uri3.1.8 through schema-utils4.5.0/Ajv8.20.0. Add a narrow compatible3.x override to reviewed3.1.9 and regenerate with declaredpnpm10.33.0; only the parser resolution and override change. Frozen installation completed in a separate task-owned root, leaving original and concurrent dependency installations untouched. Six tests resolve the actual installed schema-utils->Ajv->fast-uri chain: encoded scheme rejection, malformed host errors, relative-reference resolution, safe relative suffix serialization, and valid/invalid relative schema reference compilation. Actual old3.1.8 fails three advisory controls. The safe suffix-object fixture also passes3.1.8, so it is compatibility coverage rather than differential proof of that advisory; no application exploitability is claimed. Cheap guard pins all locked instances and the actual Ajv binding. CI/release and production acceptance remain separately tracked. Mobile ExpoZod/forge findings remain SEC004.

verify.note: All locked fast-uri instances and Ajv binding use reviewed3.1.9. Actual consumer tests and three old-version differential controls passed separately; no production exploit or release claim.
